references.text: Joseph tells his brothers that what they intended for evil against him, God intended for good to preserve many people alive – a direct parallel to his explanation in Gen 45:5 that God sent him to Egypt.
The psalmist describes how God sent Joseph ahead of His people to Egypt and how he was sold as a slave – part of God's plan to preserve His people.

Stephen recounts that the patriarchs sold Joseph out of jealousy, but that God was with him, rescued him from all his troubles, and gave him favor and wisdom in Pharaoh's sight – confirming God's plan through Joseph's sale.
Joseph expands on what he said in verse 5: God sent him ahead to preserve a remnant on earth and keep them alive, and it was not his brothers but God who sent him to Egypt.
Paul's teaching that all things work together for good for those who love God reflects the same principle Joseph expressed: God's sovereign plan works even through evil actions.
Both verses illustrate how God can turn human grief and mistakes into a means of salvation and repentance.
Both verses highlight God's specific promise to save the life of those who trust in Him during a deadly crisis.
